name: The Archaeological Heritage of Niah National Park’s Caves Complex
description: In the rainforest of Niah National Park, near Borneo's west coast in Sarawak, a network of enormous linked caverns holds traces of human life stretching back at least 50,000 years. Visitors can see prehistoric rock paintings and boat-shaped burials near the northern edge of the limestone massif. Local people still follow the custom of molong, taking only what they need when gathering bird's nests and guano.
